{"body":"
### Added

- **`sequant merge --check` warns about open PRs outside the batch that touch the batch's files (#1454).** A new `external-pr-overlap` check lists each open PR on origin whose changed files intersect the batch's, as one warning naming the PR number, head branch and shared paths. PRs whose head branch is in the batch are excluded. The warnings never change the batch verdict or the exit code. When `gh` is unavailable or the PR list call fails, the report shows one `Open-PR overlap check skipped: <reason>` line. The file lists come from a new `GitHubProvider.listOpenPRFilesSync`, and `assess-collision-detect.ts` gains `formatOpenPrCollisionWarnings`, which `/assess` will call once the plugin freeze lifts. See ADR-0016.
- **Standalone `sequant ready` records its run to `.sequant/metrics.json` (#929).** One `MetricRun` per gate pass with `source: "ready"`, the policy in `flags`, `success`/`failed` from the gate result, `qaIterations`, `tokensUsed` and the effort/model escalations. Recording is best-effort: a write failure warns on stderr and leaves the exit code and `--json` stdout alone. `sequant stats` reports `bySource` counts, and headline averages cover `run` records only. Records with no `source` read as `run`; no migration.
- **The `main` ruleset payload uses a merge queue instead of strict up-to-date (#1350).** `scripts/ruleset-main.sh --print` now drops `strict_required_status_checks_policy`, adds a squash `merge_queue` rule and lists `canary` beside `test` (the live ruleset already required both). `ci.yml` runs on `merge_group` so queued PRs get their checks. The live ruleset is unchanged: applying the queue waits on #1368, where `/release` learns to wait for a queued merge before tagging.
- **`/exec` and `/qa` run the tests a branch affects instead of the full suite (#1349).** `npx vitest run --changed origin/main` (jest: `--changedSince`), plus AC `Evidence:` test files, changed test files and tests that mention a changed file. Stacks with no affected mode keep the full command (`resolveAffectedTestCommand`). CI still runs everything.
- **gitleaks scans every PR for the leak classes generic scanners miss (#1352).** `.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml` runs a pinned, checksum-verified gitleaks with `.gitleaks.toml` on `pull_request` and `merge_group`, and fails when an `entire/*` ref exists on `origin`. Project rules flag real home paths (`/Users/<name>/`, `/home/<name>/`) and Claude session links and ids; placeholder names are allowlisted by name. `scripts/gitleaks-precommit.sh` is an optional local gate that also loads an untracked `.gitleaks.local.toml`. GitHub secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot security updates are now enabled on the repo. The committed eval results and two test files no longer carry a real home path or session id. See `docs/reference/secret-scanning.md`.
- **`/qa` enforces a follow-up ledger, and the PR body lists QA's follow-ups (#1249).** Every item an earlier phase deferred (spec's Open Questions and out-of-scope notes, exec's PR-body follow-ups, QA's own `document` findings) must end `filed #N`, `fixed in this PR` or `dropped: <reason>`. An unresolved item caps the verdict at `AC_MET_BUT_NOT_A_PLUS` through a new §7 gate, `followup_ledger_status`, in both Standard and Simple Fix mode. QA writes each `document` finding's resolution as a suffix on its description, and `sequant run`'s PR body renders the latest QA pass's `document` findings as a `## Follow-ups` checklist; a finding with no resolution reads `unresolved`. The sibling-site scan now names the defect class it searched (e.g. "every git call without `-C <target>`") rather than searching for the changed code, and an AC that promises end-to-end delivery (e.g. "surfaces in the PR body") can no longer be marked MET with that path under "Not tested": QA runs it or marks the AC PENDING. `qa/SKILL.md` did not grow. See ADR-0007.
- **A PR from a `sequant run` that QA has not reviewed says so (#1246).** The automated PR body carries one line, `> **QA has not run** — phases run: spec, exec. …`, until QA has reviewed the latest exec: a qa pass after the run's last exec, or, in a run with no exec, a qa an earlier run completed (`--resume` past qa). The post-QA update replaces it with the verdict note, or drops it for `READY_FOR_MERGE`, and a later qa-only run on the same PR removes it too. A run that skips qa (`--phases exec`, MCP `phases: "spec,exec"`) or stops before it keeps the line. No draft PRs; the PR-creation gate is unchanged. The MCP `sequant_run` `phases` description no longer offers `'spec,exec'` as a way to "skip QA".

### Changed

- **`update` refuses on a skills-only install (#1482).** It read no install scope, so it wrote hooks, agents and `settings.json` over an install that chose skills only. On a partial scope it now writes nothing, exits non-zero and names `sequant sync --only skills`. Full installs are unchanged. ADR-0015 amended.
- **The `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` floor is `^0.3.296` (#1440).** Phase agents run the Claude Code bundled with the SDK (2.1.296 at 0.3.296), not the installed `claude`, so a fresh install can no longer resolve a bundle older than the 2.1.290–2.1.296 fixes (remote MCP reconnect backoff, `.mcp.json` servers switched off for a folder, `rate_limit_event` extra-usage flag, file-read-state, `disableClaudeAiConnectors` / `allowedMcpServers` coverage). The README Prerequisites note says which Claude Code a phase agent runs.

### Removed

- **Dead `src/lib/plugin-version-sync.ts` module and its test (#1325).** Nothing in production called `checkVersionSync`; CI's `Check version sync` step does the check. `docs/internal/plugin-updates.md` now names that step.

### Fixed

- **`sequant_run` no longer reports another run's issues and verdict when its own run log is missing (#1515).** A runId lookup miss fell back to the newest log in the time window, so parallel runs whose log was never written showed a sibling run's result. `resolveRunLog` now retries the exact runId lookup (3 × 200 ms) and returns `null` on a miss; the response carries `runLogMissing`, `requestedIssues` and a `note` saying the result is not a parsed log. The no-runId path is unchanged.
- **`new-feature.sh` reuses the issue's local branch when no worktree has it (#1491).** It printed advice (one option was `git branch -D`) and exited 1, while `ensureWorktree` checks the branch out as is. It now runs `git worktree add <path> <branch>` with no fetch or reset, like the TS side, and keeps a recorded `sequantBase`. The existing-worktree lookup matches the branch exactly, so `feature/7-x` no longer matches `feature/7-xy`.
- **`doctor` Skills Version check warns on content drift (#1490).** At a matching version it always passed with `Up to date`, while the pre-flight banner in the same run reported differing files. It now warns with the file count and the banner's remedy, which both read from one function.
- **`doctor` no longer sends a skills-only install to `init --force` (#1489).** A missing `AGENTS.md` raised a warning naming `sequant init --force`, which installs hooks, agents and settings the install skipped. On a partial scope the check now passes and says `AGENTS.md` is outside the install. Full installs keep the warning.
- **`sequant merge --check` works on a repo whose default branch is not `main` (#1484).** The combined-branch test, each branch's `filesModified` diff, overlap detection and the residual pattern scan all hard-coded `origin/main`. On a `master` repo the diffs failed, their callers read the empty output as "no changes", and the overlap checks (including #1454's external-PR overlap) reported clean. `runMergeChecks` now resolves `origin/<default branch>` once and passes it to all four. A failed `filesModified` diff is no longer an empty list: the report carries an error finding for that branch naming the git command, and the batch is `BLOCKED`. The worktree path of `resolveBranches` also uses the resolved base instead of `main`.
- **Plain `sync` and `doctor` no longer steer a skills-only install into a full one (#1485).** A plain `sync` on a manifest with `groups: ["skills"]` keeps that scope: it counts drift and writes only `.claude/skills/`, and widening is `sequant init`. `doctor`'s Skills Version check names `sync --only skills`, and `doctor` advises the `"groups": ["skills"]` hand edit for a legacy manifest with no hooks, settings or agents. See ADR-0015.
- **`sequant run` reuses an issue's existing branch whatever the issue's title (#1487).** The branch was looked up by a name rebuilt from the title. A failed `gh issue view` (title `Issue #N`) or a retitled issue therefore cut a second branch, `feature/N-issue-n`, from the base, and QA reviewed the base instead of the PR. `ensureWorktree` now finds the issue's branch by number: a local `feature/N-*` (which covers worktrees) or `origin/feature/N-*`. One match is reused. With several matches, the one the title names is used. Otherwise no worktree is created and every candidate is listed. When the title could not be read, a non-dry run now prints a warning that names the issue and the `gh` error.
- **`new-feature.sh` starts from `origin/<branch>` when the remote already has the issue's branch (#1486).** It always cut the worktree from `origin/<base>`, so a pushed PR branch lost its commits and a push from the new worktree diverged. The script now ports `resolveBranchStartRef`: it uses `origin/<branch>` unless that branch is merged into the base (merge commit or squash), and `--print-start-ref <branch> <base-ref>` exposes the result for the parity test.
- **An issue whose worktree could not be created fails, and no longer runs its phases in the main checkout (#1469).** When `git worktree add` failed, `sequant run` dropped the issue from the worktree map and ran spec, exec and QA in the main checkout on whatever branch was checked out there. Under worktree isolation the issue now fails before any phase runs, and its `abortReason` and the run log carry git's stderr. `IssueExecutionContext` gets an explicit `worktreeRequired` flag, because a missing `worktree` also means "isolation off". The provisioning summary counts failures (`N created, M reused, K failed`). Two CLIs provisioning in one repo race on `.git/config.lock`. A `could not lock config file` failure is now retried up to 5 times with 100–800 ms backoff, and a retry adds the branch the failed `-b` attempt already created. `recordWorktreeBaseRef` uses the same retry and warns on a final failure instead of swallowing it.
- **Phase agents get `SEQUANT_BASE_BRANCH` (#1460).** `sequant run` never set it, so skills that read `${SEQUANT_BASE_BRANCH:-main}` always used `main`, and on a repository whose default branch is `master` every `origin/main` in a phase's git commands failed. Every phase, spec included, now gets the base branch name from `resolveBaseRef`. When no base is recorded, `resolveBaseRef` falls back to `origin/<default branch>` of the repository it reads, not a literal `origin/main`.
- **Uncommitted changes to `.claude/hooks/` now trigger the same warning as uncommitted skills (#1456).** Phase worktrees check out the committed hooks, so a `sync` that rewrote `pre-tool.sh` and was never committed left every phase on the old guard logic with no signal. `getSkillsCommitState` lists tracked-but-modified files under both directories, and the shared warning names each directory. Untracked hooks stay silent. `run`, `doctor` and `sync` print it through their existing call sites.
- **A worktree for a non-default bare base (`--base release`) is cut from `origin/<base>` after a fetch (#1406).** It was cut from the local branch, which can lag or not exist, while staleness and the recorded `sequantBaseRef` read `origin/<base>`. Creation, recreate and the record now share one ref. Stacked predecessors and bases with no `origin/<base>` stay local.
- **A `SEQUANT_MUTATION` marker whose text contains `}` no longer parses to nothing (#1305).** The parser matched to the first `}`, so a `mutation` such as `regex changed to /x{9}/` made the marker vanish from QA §6i and from the exec carry-over. It now matches to the ` -->` terminator, and `renderMutationMarker` escapes `-->` and `<!--` inside a value so it round-trips. Existing markers, including ones whose JSON spans lines or whose values hold an HTML comment, parse as before.
- **A skills-only install no longer warns about files it never installed, and its remedy no longer overwrites the constitution (#1409).** After `init --manifest-only` + `sync --only skills`, every command warned `N file(s) differ` for the hooks, agents, `scripts/dev` and `.claude/settings.json` the install left out, and suggested `sync --force`, which overwrites `.claude/memory/constitution.md`. `.sequant-manifest.json` now records the install scope in a `groups` field (`init --manifest-only` writes `[]`, `sync --only skills` adds `"skills"`, a full sync of a manifest without a scope removes it; `update` refuses on a partial scope). Drift is counted only inside that scope, and the remedy is `sync --only skills --force`. A manifest without the field is a full install, so existing installs are unchanged. See ADR-0015.
- **A fresh machine's first worktree for a pushed PR branch starts from `origin/<branch>`, and a worktree already at `origin/<branch>` is not recreated on every run (#1405).** With no local branch, `ensureWorktree` cut a new branch from the base even when the remote had the PR's commits. It now starts from `origin/<branch>` with upstream tracking, unless that branch is already merged into the base (merge commit or squash) or was deleted from the remote. A stale, clean worktree whose HEAD equals `origin/<branch>` is reused instead of being deleted and re-added. The check uses local `git` only, with no `gh` call. See ADR-0014.
- **Phase agents no longer receive the user's claude.ai connectors (#1396).** The Claude Code driver passes `settings: { disableClaudeAiConnectors: true }` to `query()`, so Gmail, Docs and other account connectors the SDK adds outside the #936 allowlist are not reachable from a `bypassPermissions` phase agent. The `sequant` server, `.mcp.json` servers and `mcpAllowlist` names are unaffected.
- **A stale worktree for a pushed PR branch is recreated from `origin/<branch>`, not from the base (#1380).** When a worktree was more than 5 commits behind and clean, `ensureWorktree` deleted the local branch and cut a new one from the base, so a qa re-run reviewed the base without the PR's commits. The recreate now starts from `origin/<branch>` when the remote has it. If the start ref does not contain the worktree's HEAD (an offline fetch, or a local-only branch with commits of its own), it prints a warning and keeps the existing worktree. See ADR-0013.
- **First-run papercuts from a stranger smoke test (#1387).** The "Running sequant from local node_modules" warning no longer tells a project that declares `sequant` in `package.json` to uninstall it (a stray, undeclared install still warns). `init`'s next steps now say to commit the generated files and run `npx sequant run <issue>`. `doctor`'s `Warnings:` count includes the upstream #43869 notice it prints, so a healthy install now reads "All checks passed (1 warning)" unless `--quiet`. The `still running` line shows time since the current phase started, not the issue. `run --help` describes `--no-rebase` as skipping the rebase onto the base branch.
- **`sequant run --base <branch>` opens the PR against `<branch>` (#1386).** The worktree was cut from `--base` and rebased onto it, but `createPR` set `gh pr create --base` only under `--stacked`, so a plain `--base` (or `settings.run.defaultBase`) opened the PR against the repo default and its diff carried every difference between the two branches. `createPR` now takes the run's one resolved base and derives the PR target through `resolvePrBase`; `--stacked` still wins for non-last links, and a base equal to the repo default passes no `--base`, as before.
- **Uncommitted skills no longer pass silently (#1354).** `sequant run` checks phase worktrees out from git, so a `sequant sync` that was never committed never reached a phase, and the `Skills are outdated` warning, which reads the on-disk version, named a version the phases weren't using. `sequant run` (before provisioning worktrees), `doctor`, `sync` and `update` now warn when tracked files under `.claude/skills/` have uncommitted changes, naming the committed version phases will run. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#phases-behave-like-an-older-sequant-after-sync).
- Worktree provisioning's skip message now says `no package.json at the worktree root` for JS stacks, so a repo whose package lives in a subdirectory sees why nothing installed. The `npm ci` EUSAGE itself was fixed by #1196 (#1243)
- **The run dashboard shows phases in the order they run (#1356).** When label detection adds a phase to `--phases` (e.g. `exec,qa` gains `test`), the dashboard's issue card listed it last, after `qa`, because the orchestrator never applied the resolved phase plan the plain-text renderer already used. It now does, so `exec ▸ test ▸ qa` reads correctly from the start, and a configured phase the plan dropped no longer lingers as pending.
- **`.sequant-manifest.json` ends with a newline (#1355).** `sequant init`, `sync` and `update` wrote the manifest with no final newline, so a repo whose CI runs `prettier --check` failed after every sync.
- **Parallel runs (every MCP `sequant_run`) no longer drop per-issue warnings (#1342).** `runIssueWithLogging` silenced all per-issue output in parallel mode, including warnings: the spec-recommendation parse failure, "PR after exec failed", the checkpoint-commit failure, relay and ready-gate warnings, and evidence bundles. They now go through a `warn` channel built on `bracketedConsoleLog`, which uses the renderer's `appendNotice` under the TUI and `console.log` otherwise. Progress lines stay suppressed.
- **The recommended Claude Code version is now 2.1.288 (#1346).** Sequant relies on Claude Code's native dangerous-`rm` analyzer, which before 2.1.288 let a `bash -c` or `sh -c` script run a dangerous `rm` without a prompt under `bypassPermissions`, the mode phase agents run in. The README gives the new recommendation and the reason, and `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` lists the analyzer as a defense with that version dependency. ADR-0009 (#1345) is accepted.
- **`/verify` ignores Claude Code's pre-commit nudge (#1345).** Claude Code ≥ 2.1.286 tells Claude to run any project skill named `verify` before committing, and Sequant ships one that expects an issue number and posts to GitHub. `/verify` now returns a one-line no-op, with no command, comment or question, when a Sequant phase other than verify calls it (checked through `SEQUANT_PHASE`, even with an issue number), when it gets no issue number, or when Claude calls it on its own before a commit. A `/verify <N>` you ask for, and the verify phase, run as before. `sequant update` / `sync` deliver the guard to existing projects. `/upstream` now files changelog lines that name a skill Sequant ships under a new **Name Collision** category instead of No Action, and warns if it cannot find the shipped skill list. See ADR-0009.
- **The `sequant run` PR body carries exec's `## Summary` again (#1311).** The Claude Code, Codex and opencode drivers joined the agent's text messages with no separator, so a message ending mid-line ("Now the edits.") glued onto exec's final `## Summary` and the line-anchored heading was never found; the PR got the placeholder body even though exec wrote a full summary (4 of 4 runs on 2026-10-05). Messages now start on their own line. The placeholder warning also printed nowhere under the MCP server, because per-issue logging is off in parallel mode; it now prints there and names the exec output's length, so "exec wrote nothing" and "exec's summary was missed" read differently.
- **`/release` bumps the plugin manifest users install (#1301).** Step 4.5 edited and staged the root `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, which nothing installs; the shipped `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` was bumped only by `scripts/release.sh`. The root manifest is retired: `/release` (validate, bump, `git add`, summary), `scripts/release.sh`, `scripts/prepare-marketplace.ts`, `plugin-version-sync.ts` and the CI plugin checks now read `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, the one manifest. `plugin-install-test.yml` now triggers on `templates/memory/**`, the source of the shipped `plugin/memory/`, instead of the repo's own root `memory/`.
- **`/qa`, `/clean` and `/setup` no longer pre-approve file-deleting or API wildcards (#1292).** `/qa` drops `Bash(gh api:*)`, which also allowed `gh api -X DELETE`. `/clean` drops `Bash(rm:*)` and `Bash(find:*)`, and narrows `Bash(mv:*)` to moves into `docs/archive/` and `scripts/archive/`. `/setup` narrows `Bash(cp:*)`, `Bash(cat:*)` and `Bash(sed:*)` to the files it writes or reads. When you run these skills by hand, the removed commands now ask for permission; `sequant run` phases are unaffected. The #1287 gate test now also rejects `Bash(<tool>:*)` for `gh api`, `rm`, `mv`, `find`, `sed` and `cp`, unless an allowlist entry gives a reason.
- **The docs no longer cite the 44% second-look figure (#1309).** `docs/reference/ready-command.md`, `docs/features/run-ready-gate.md`, `docs/investigations/ready-gate-backtest.md` and `docs/internal/what-weve-built.md` now give the figure rebuilt from the surviving transcripts: 10 of 27 second looks caught a would-ship bug, 7 of them only after the human's "any gaps?" follow-up and 3 in the first verdict. They link `docs/investigations/qa-second-look-dataset.md`, and no longer state that the in-orchestrator QA under-catches, which the transcripts cannot show.
- **A failed `gh` call no longer reads as a posted comment or label (#1312).** `GitHubProvider.postComment`, `addLabel` and `removeLabel` ran `spawnSync` and never looked at the result, so a non-zero exit, a timeout or a failed spawn resolved as success and `postQaVerdictComment`'s "Failed to post QA verdict comment" warning could never fire. They now throw with `gh`'s stderr, so a lost QA verdict is logged.
- **`postPRComment` no longer fails silently, and the ready gate no longer swallows a failed report post (#1315).** `GitHubProvider.postPRComment` had the same unchecked `spawnSync` as #1312 and now throws with `gh`'s stderr. The ready gate's `postReport` catch was empty; it now logs `Failed to post ready-gate report for #N: <error>` (through the new optional `log` option, default `console.warn`) and stays non-fatal. `PlatformProvider`'s doc comment now states the contract: every async method rejects on failure, except `checkAuth`, which answers `false`. `getIssueComments` now follows it and rejects instead of resolving `[]` when `gh` fails.
- **Skills no longer break when Claude Code substitutes `$0`/`$1` in their text (#1289).** Claude Code replaces positional `$N` in a skill's body when the skill gets arguments, and fenced code blocks are not exempt: `/qa 1249` turned `substr($0, 2)` into `substr(1249, 2)`, silently breaking §6c's added-line extraction and the manual-AC attribution program. Awk fields in the shipped skills are now written `$(N)`, which Claude Code leaves alone and which also works for drivers that read the files untemplated (codex, opencode). The §6c extraction moved to `qa/scripts/added-lines.sh`. A new CI lint, `npm run lint:skill-argument-substitution`, rejects any `$N` in a SKILL.md body, escaped or not.
- **A ladder halt is recorded, not only printed (#1254).** When a run halts on `SPEC_DIVERGENCE`, `DIVERGENCE_SUSPECT` or `TOP_OF_LADDER`, the issue result carries the failure category `ladder_halt`, an `abortReason` such as `ladder halt: SPEC_DIVERGENCE in exec (AC-2)` and the evidence bundle; the run log's issue entry records `failure` with the same reason and bundle. A phase that declared `SPEC_DIVERGENCE` now reads failed in state (with `outcome` and `divergenceAcs`), in its run-log row and in its progress event, even when the agent exited cleanly. The MCP `sequant_run` result names `haltReason`, `declaredAcs` and `abortReason` per issue. Any other failure no failed phase accounts for (e.g. a rebase-conflict abort) is now also logged `failure` with its `abortReason`, instead of `success`.
- **Under `sequant run`, phase agents no longer edit the PR body (#1302).** A quality-loop exec had rewritten a PR's body itself (`gh api` PATCH), because QA's missing-marker gap pointed at the PR body. That body then read as hand-edited, and every later sequant update (QA verdict note, follow-ups) was dropped. The exec skill now forbids changing the PR's body or title by any means under the orchestrator, and routes the AC table, mutation markers, settle-against-base blocks and hook-verdict changes into its final `## Summary`, which the orchestrator carries into the body. QA's §6i `Missing` gap names exec's final Summary, not the PR body.
- **The `sequant run` PR body keeps exec's mutation markers and AC table when exec wrote no `## Summary` (#1297).** The body now carries every valid `SEQUANT_MUTATION` marker from exec's final output, including markers exec fenced in a code block (outside the 4,000-character cap, never duplicated) and, with no Summary, the AC table; the placeholder only appears when there is nothing to carry, and the run output warns when it does. The issue state's stored summary carries the markers too, so a qa-only re-run's PR update keeps them.
- Skills no longer pre-approve broad shell access in `allowed-tools` (#1287). Bare `Bash` (`/fullsolve`, `/loop`, `/test`), `Bash(*)` (`/verify`), tool wildcards such as `Bash(git *)` and `Bash(gh *)` (`/assess`, `/solve`, `/improve`, `/upstream`, `/merger`), and runner wildcards such as `Bash(npx tsc:*)` and `Bash(node -e:*)` are replaced by the subcommands each skill runs, or removed. `/test`'s unrendered `Bash({{PM_RUN}} dev:*)` becomes literal `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` dev entries. When you run these skills by hand, commands outside their list now ask for permission; `sequant run` phases are unaffected. A new gate test rejects these forms in all four skill copies.
- `/qa` §6i counts changed `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `*.yaml` files in its diff-file list, so a `SEQUANT_MUTATION` marker naming a CI workflow step classifies `valid` instead of `test_not_in_diff` (#1276)
- A quality loop that ends `qa AC_NOT_MET → loop → qa NEEDS_VERIFICATION` records `awaiting_verification` instead of `ready_for_merge`, and the PR-body QA note and the MCP `sequant_run` result (`verdict`, `acMet`/`acTotal`, `gaps`, `findings`) report the latest qa pass, not the first (#1245). The latest-attempt accessor moved to `src/lib/workflow/latest-phase.ts`; the failed-phase scans in `deriveFailureCategory` and `run-display.ts` use it too


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/sequant-io/sequant/compare/v2.19.0...v2.20.0
